description: The baseline is the average modulation index over all linked signals, with every signal counting equally.

b.request: Compute the average modulation index across all signals that successfully link to a telescope and observatory, weighting each linked signal equally. For each telescope and weather profile, compute the average modulation index and phase shift, retaining only groups whose average modulation index exceeds that overall baseline. Then, for each weather profile, report the average modulation index and phase shift across the retained groups and the average difference between their group modulation indices and the overall baseline, without rounding
b.sql:
WITH linked_signals AS (
  SELECT s.modindex, s.phaseshiftdeg, t.telescregistry, o.weathprofile
  FROM signals AS s
  JOIN telescopes AS t ON t.telescregistry = s.telescref
  JOIN observatories AS o ON o.observstation = t.observstation
), baseline AS (
  SELECT AVG(modindex) AS overall_avg_modindex
  FROM linked_signals
), telescope_weather_groups AS (
  SELECT telescregistry, weathprofile,
         AVG(modindex) AS avg_modindex,
         AVG(phaseshiftdeg) AS avg_phaseshiftdeg
  FROM linked_signals
  GROUP BY telescregistry, weathprofile
), retained_groups AS (
  SELECT g.*, b.overall_avg_modindex
  FROM telescope_weather_groups AS g
  CROSS JOIN baseline AS b
  WHERE g.avg_modindex > b.overall_avg_modindex
)
SELECT weathprofile,
       AVG(avg_modindex) AS avg_modindex,
       AVG(avg_phaseshiftdeg) AS avg_phaseshiftdeg,
       AVG(avg_modindex - overall_avg_modindex) AS avg_modindex_difference_from_baseline
FROM retained_groups
GROUP BY weathprofile;

c.request: Linking signals to their telescopes and observatories (signals that don't match are dropped), find the average modulation index and average phase shift for each telescope and weather profile (`weathprofile`). Keep the telescope/weather groups whose modulation index is above the overall average modulation index. Then, per weather profile, show the average modulation index and average phase shift of those groups, and how far above the overall average they are on average. Don't round anything. The baseline is the average modulation index over all linked signals, with every signal counting equally.
c.sql:
WITH linked_signals AS (
  SELECT s.modindex, s.phaseshiftdeg, t.telescregistry, o.weathprofile
  FROM signals AS s
  JOIN telescopes AS t ON s.telescref = t.telescregistry
  JOIN observatories AS o ON t.observstation = o.observstation
), baseline AS (
  SELECT AVG(modindex) AS overall_avg_modindex
  FROM linked_signals
), qualifying_groups AS (
  SELECT ls.telescregistry, ls.weathprofile,
         AVG(ls.modindex) AS avg_modindex,
         AVG(ls.phaseshiftdeg) AS avg_phaseshift
  FROM linked_signals AS ls
  GROUP BY ls.telescregistry, ls.weathprofile
  HAVING AVG(ls.modindex) > (SELECT overall_avg_modindex FROM baseline)
)
SELECT qg.weathprofile,
       AVG(qg.avg_modindex) AS avg_modindex,
       AVG(qg.avg_phaseshift) AS avg_phaseshift,
       AVG(qg.avg_modindex - b.overall_avg_modindex) AS avg_above_overall_modindex
FROM qualifying_groups AS qg
CROSS JOIN baseline AS b
GROUP BY qg.weathprofile;

a.request: Link each signal to its telescope and that telescope's observatory, dropping signals that don't match. For each telescope and weather profile (`weathprofile`), work out the average modulation index and the average phase shift. Keep the telescope/weather groups whose average modulation index is above the average modulation index across all linked signals, with each signal counting equally. Then for each weather profile, return the weather profile, the average of the kept groups' average modulation index, the average of their average phase shift, and the average amount by which their modulation index is above that baseline. Don't round anything.
a.sql:
WITH linked_signals AS (
  SELECT s.modindex, s.phaseshiftdeg, o.weathprofile, s.telescref
  FROM signals AS s
  INNER JOIN telescopes AS t ON t.telescregistry = s.telescref
  INNER JOIN observatories AS o ON o.observstation = t.observstation
), baseline AS (
  SELECT AVG(modindex) AS avg_modindex
  FROM linked_signals
), telescope_weather AS (
  SELECT telescref, weathprofile,
         AVG(modindex) AS avg_modindex,
         AVG(phaseshiftdeg) AS avg_phaseshift
  FROM linked_signals
  GROUP BY telescref, weathprofile
), kept_groups AS (
  SELECT tw.*,
         tw.avg_modindex - b.avg_modindex AS above_baseline
  FROM telescope_weather AS tw
  CROSS JOIN baseline AS b
  WHERE tw.avg_modindex > b.avg_modindex
)
SELECT weathprofile,
       AVG(avg_modindex) AS avg_modulation_index,
       AVG(avg_phaseshift) AS avg_phase_shift,
       AVG(above_baseline) AS avg_modulation_index_above_baseline
FROM kept_groups
GROUP BY weathprofile;

d.request: Using the average modulation index across all linked signals, with each signal weighted equally, as the baseline, show for each weather profile the average modulation index and average phase shift of telescope/weather groups whose modulation index exceeds that baseline, plus the average amount by which those groups exceed it. Do not round any values.
d.sql:
WITH group_averages AS (
  SELECT
    o.weathprofile,
    s.telescref,
    AVG(s.modindex) AS avg_modulation_index,
    AVG(s.phaseshiftdeg) AS avg_phase_shift
  FROM signals AS s
  JOIN telescopes AS t ON t.telescregistry = s.telescref
  JOIN observatories AS o ON o.observstation = t.observstation
  GROUP BY o.weathprofile, s.telescref
),
baseline AS (
  SELECT AVG(modindex) AS avg_modulation_index
  FROM signals
)
SELECT
  g.weathprofile,
  g.telescref,
  g.avg_modulation_index,
  g.avg_phase_shift,
  g.avg_modulation_index - b.avg_modulation_index AS amount_above_baseline
FROM group_averages AS g
CROSS JOIN baseline AS b
WHERE g.avg_modulation_index > b.avg_modulation_index;
